p.src: Pinger came out and instructed Lin Zhixiao's wife: “A thriving household turns great troubles into small ones and small troubles into nothing at all. It makes no sense to raise a deafening uproar over every trifling matter one cannot settle. Take the mother and daughter back now and let them resume their former duties. Send Qin Xian's wife back to her former post. There is no need ever to mention this affair again. What matters is that you patrol and inspect the place carefully every day.” With that, she rose and left. Mrs. Liu and her daughter hastened forward to kowtow. Lin Zhixiao's wife took them back to the garden and reported to Li Wan and Tanchun, who both said, “We understand. It is best that nothing more should come of it.” Thus Siqi and the others had been excited for nothing. Qin Xian's wife had waited a long time for this opening and wormed her way into it, only to enjoy her triumph for half a day. She was in the kitchen amid the confusion of taking over utensils, grain, coal, and other supplies when she discovered many shortages as well. “Two shi of polished rice are missing, a whole extra month's supply of ordinary rice has been drawn, and the coal is below its proper quota,” she said. Meanwhile she prepared gifts for Lin Zhixiao's wife: secretly setting aside a basket of coal, five hundred jin of firewood, and a shoulder-load of polished rice, she had her nephews take them from outside straight to the Lin household. She also prepared a gift for the accounts office and several vegetable dishes for her new colleagues, saying, “Now that I am here, I shall depend entirely upon your support. From now on, we are all one family. If I overlook anything, I beg you all to help see to it.” In the midst of all this bustle, someone suddenly came and told her, “Once you have seen to this breakfast, you are to leave. Sister Liu has been cleared of wrongdoing, so the kitchen is being returned to her charge.” At this, Qin Xian's wife felt as though her soul had been blasted from her body. Crestfallen, she instantly furled her banners, silenced her drums, bundled her things, and departed. All the things she had given away were wasted, and she now had to sell her own possessions to make good the shortages. Even Siqi was so furious she nearly fell backward, but there was no way to reverse the decision, and she had to let the matter drop. Aunt Zhao, meanwhile, was terrified that an inquiry would uncover the many things Caiyun had secretly given away after Yu-chuan had exposed the affair in a quarrel. Every day she anxiously sought news, her palms sweating with fear. Then Caiyun came and told her, “Baoyu has taken all the blame, so the matter is over.” Only then did Aunt Zhao set her mind at ease. But when Jia Huan heard this, he grew suspicious. He brought out everything Caiyun had secretly given him and flung it in her face, crying, “You two-faced creature! I want none of them. If you were not on intimate terms with Baoyu, why would he agree to take the blame for you? Since you had the courage to give them to me, you ought not to have told a soul. Now that you have told him, it would be shameful for me to keep them.”

p.src: Seeing him react this way, Caiyun anxiously swore oath after oath until she was in tears and tried every possible explanation, but Jia Huan stubbornly refused to believe her. “Were it not for my regard for you all this time, I would go tell Second Sister-in-law that you stole these things for me and that I dare not keep them. Think it over carefully.” With that, he flung out his hand and stalked away. In exasperation, Aunt Zhao cursed him: “You ill-starred wretch, you maggot-hearted fiend!” Caiyun was so distressed that she wept until her tears ran dry and her heart seemed torn apart. Aunt Zhao did all she could to comfort her: “My good child, he has betrayed your devotion; I can see that clearly. Let me put these things away. In a couple of days, he will naturally come round.” As she spoke, she reached to gather up the things. But Caiyun, in a fit of resentment, bundled them all together. When no one was watching, she went into the garden and threw them into the river, where some sank and others floated away with the current. Still heartsick, she wept secretly beneath her covers that night.

p.src: Baoyu's birthday now arrived, and it happened that Baoqin shared the same birthday. Because Lady Wang was away, the celebrations were not as lively as in former years. Taoist Zhang alone sent four kinds of gifts and a renewed register-name talisman. Monks and nuns from several temples also sent the tips of offerings, paper effigies of the God of Longevity and written prayers, as well as renewed annual lock-charms for his natal-star deity and the year's presiding Tai Sui. The female storytellers who regularly visited the household came to offer birthday greetings. Wang Ziteng's household sent, as usual, a complete suit of clothes, a pair of shoes and socks, one hundred longevity peaches, and one hundred bundles of fine silver-thread noodles for palace use. Aunt Xue's gifts were one degree less lavish. Among the rest of the family, Madam You again gave a pair of shoes and socks, while Xifeng gave a palace-made purse embroidered on all four sides with symbols of harmonious union; inside it were a golden God of Longevity and a plaything made in Persia. People were sent to the various temples to distribute alms in their halls. There were separate gifts for Baoqin as well, too many to describe in detail. The young ladies exchanged only casual tokens: one might give a fan, another a piece of calligraphy, a painting, or a poem—merely something suitable to the occasion.

p.src: Early that morning, Baoyu rose, washed and combed his hair, then put on his cap and formal dress and came out. When he reached the courtyard before the front hall, Li Gui and four or five others had already set out incense and candles for Heaven and Earth. Baoyu lit an incense stick. After completing the rites, offering tea, and burning paper, he went to the ancestral shrine and the Hall of the Ancestors in the Ning mansion and performed the ceremonies at both places. Coming out onto the terrace, he faced upward and bowed from afar to Grandmother Jia, Jia Zheng, Lady Wang, and the others. He then went directly to Madam You's main rooms, paid his respects, sat for a while, and only afterward returned to the Rong mansion. First he visited Aunt Xue, who repeatedly tried to keep him there. Then he met Xue Ke and exchanged courtesies with him before finally entering the garden. Qingwen and Sheyue followed him, while a little maid carried a felt mat under her arm. Beginning with Li Wan, he visited each of his elders in turn in their rooms. He then went out through the second gate and exchanged courtesies at the homes of his four wet nurses, Li, Zhao, Zhang, and Wang, before coming back inside. Although everyone wished to bow formally to him, he would not accept their obeisance. When he returned to his room, Xiren and the others merely came over and offered their good wishes. Lady Wang had said that young people should not receive formal obeisance, lest it diminish their good fortune and longevity; therefore none of them kowtowed.

p.src: No wonder she is so blessed—her birthday comes before everyone else's. It is also the birthday of our imperial ancestor. After the Lantern Festival come the Old Lady and Sister Bao; mother and daughter happened upon dates close together. The first day of the third month is Madam's birthday, and the ninth is Cousin Lian's. There is no one in the second month.” Xiren said, “Miss Lin's birthday is on the twelfth day of the second month. How can you say there is no one? It is only that she is not a member of our household.” Tanchun laughed. “What has become of my memory!” Pointing at Xiren, Baoyu said with a laugh, “She shares a birthday with Cousin Lin, so she remembers it.” Tanchun laughed. “So the two of you share a birthday. Yet every year you do not even come and kowtow to us once. We did not know Pinger's birthday either; we have only just learned of it today.” Pinger smiled. “What standing have people like us? We have neither the good fortune to receive birthday obeisances nor the rank to accept presents. Why make a commotion? Naturally we let the day pass quietly. But today she had to go and announce it. When you young ladies return to your rooms, I shall come and pay my respects.” Tanchun laughed. “There is no need to trouble yourself. But today we really must celebrate your birthday, or my conscience will not be at ease.” Baoyu, Xiangyun, and the others all agreed, “Quite right.” Tanchun then instructed a maid, “Go and tell her mistress that we have all agreed not to let Pinger leave us for the whole day. We are pooling our contributions to celebrate her birthday.” The maid went off laughing and returned after some time with this message: “Second Mistress Lian says she thanks the young ladies for doing Pinger such honor. She does not know what delicacies you will give her for her birthday, but so long as you do not forget Second Mistress Lian, she will not come and pester her.” Everyone laughed. Tanchun sent people to consult Li Wan, Baochai, and Daiyu, while also summoning Mrs. Liu and ordering her to prepare two banquet tables quickly in the inner kitchen. p.src: As soon as they entered the side gate, Baochai ordered an old maid to lock it and took charge of the key herself. Baoyu quickly said, “Why bother shutting this gate? Hardly anyone uses it. Besides, Auntie and you sisters are all staying inside. Would it not be troublesome if any of you needed to go home for something?” Baochai smiled. “One cannot be too careful. Look at your side: despite all the commotion there these past few days, none of our people has been involved. That proves locking this gate has served its purpose. If it were left open, those people might take the convenient shortcut through here. Who could stop them? Better to lock it and restrict Mother and me as well, so that none of us uses it. Then, even if something happens, no one can blame anybody on our side.” Baoyu laughed. “So you too know that things have recently gone missing on our side?” Baochai smiled. “You know only about the rose dew and the poria cream, and only because the inquiry into the people involved led to those things. Had it not been for those people, you would not even know about these two items. Little do you realize that there are several other matters more serious than either of these. If they never come to light, it will be a blessing for everyone; but if they are unearthed, who knows how many people inside will be implicated? I tell you only because you take no part in managing affairs. Ping’er is sensible, so I told her the other day as well. Her mistress was not out attending to matters, and that was why I made sure Ping’er understood. If nothing emerges, everyone will be glad to let the matter drop. But if it does come out, she already has the facts clear in her mind and will know where to begin, so no innocent person will be wronged. Just heed what I say and be more watchful and careful from now on. You must not repeat this to anyone else.”

Just heed what I say and be more watchful and careful from now on. You must not repeat this to anyone else.”

p.src: She had barely entered the garden when several maids came looking for her and accompanied her to the Red Fragrance Garden. There she found tortoiseshell-patterned banquet tables spread and hibiscus-patterned cushions laid out. Everyone laughed. “Now all the birthday stars are here!” They insisted that the four places of honor should be given to the four celebrants, but all four declined. Aunt Xue said, “I am old and do not fit in with your lively young company. I would only feel constrained here. I would be better off going to the hall and lying down at my ease. I cannot eat much and scarcely drink, so it would be more convenient to leave this place to them.” Madam You and the others steadfastly refused to allow it. Baochai said, “That arrangement is fine too. Mother would indeed be more comfortable reclining at her ease in the hall, and we can send over whatever she likes to eat. Besides, no one is there in front, so she can keep an eye on things as well.” Tanchun and the others laughed. “In that case, it is better to obey than to stand on ceremony.” They all escorted her to the council hall and watched while the maids spread a brocade mattress and arranged a backrest, a long pillow, and the like. Then they instructed them, “Massage Auntie’s legs properly, and if she asks for tea or water, do not shirk your duties with excuses. When we send food over later, Auntie will reward you with whatever she leaves. Just do not leave here and go elsewhere.” The young maids all assented. Only then did Tanchun and the others return. In the end, Baoqin and Xiuyan were seated in the places of honor, with Ping’er facing west and Baoyu facing east. Tanchun also fetched Yuanyang, and the two sat shoulder to shoulder opposite them to keep them company. At a table to the west sat Baochai, Daiyu, Xiangyun, Yingchun, and Xichun; they also pulled Xiangling and Yu-chuan’er over to sit crosswise at the end. At the third table, Madam You and Li Wan drew Xiren and Caiyun in to join them. At the fourth table, Zijuan, Ying’er, Qingwen, Xiaoluo, Siqi, and the others sat in a circle. Tanchun and the others were about to offer ceremonial cups of wine, but Baoqin and the other three all protested, “If we make such a fuss, we shall never get seated all day.” So they finally desisted. Two female storytellers proposed singing ballads in celebration, but everyone said, “None of us wants to hear those rustic tales. Go to the hall and perform for Auntie to relieve her boredom.” At the same time, they selected various foods and ordered them sent to Aunt Xue. Baoyu then said, “Merely sitting decorously is dull. We ought to play a drinking game.” Some proposed one game, while others favored another. Daiyu said, “If you ask me, we should take brush and inkstone, write down every kind of game, roll the slips into lots, and play whichever one we draw.” Everyone declared the idea excellent. A brush, an inkstone, and decorated writing paper were brought at once. Xiangling had recently been studying poetry and practiced calligraphy every day. The sight of brush and inkstone was irresistible to her, and she hurriedly rose from her seat, saying, “I’ll write them.” After thinking for a while, they came up with a dozen or so games and called them out. Xiangling wrote down each one, rolled the slips into lots, and tossed them into a bottle.

p.src: Tanchun told Ping'er to draw one. Ping'er stirred the slips around inside, picked one out with her chopsticks, and opened it. On it were written the two characters “Guessing the Hidden Object.” Baochai laughed. “You've drawn the very ancestor of drinking games. ‘Guessing the Hidden Object’ has existed since ancient times, but its tradition has now been lost. These rules were compiled by later generations, and the game is harder than any other. Half the people here don't even know how to play. We had better discard it and draw another that both refined and ordinary folk can enjoy.” Tanchun laughed. “Now that it has been drawn, how can we discard it? Let us draw another now. If everyone can enjoy it, the others may play that one. We shall play this one.” With that, she had Xiren draw another slip, which proved to be “Finger-Guessing.” Shi Xiangyun laughed. “This one is simple, brisk, and straightforward—just to my taste. I won't play this ‘Guessing the Hidden Object.’ It only makes people hang their heads in gloomy frustration. I'm off to play finger-guessing.” Tanchun said, “She alone is breaking the rules. Sister Bao, quickly fine her a cup.” Allowing no protest, Baochai made Xiangyun drink a cup. Tanchun said, “I shall drink a cup. I am the games mistress, so there is no need for a formal proclamation; simply follow my directions.” She ordered the gaming dice and bowl brought over. “Beginning with Cousin Qin, throw in turn. Any two who cast the same number will play Guessing the Hidden Object.” Baoqin threw a three. Xiuyan, Baoyu, and the others all failed to match it, until at last Xiangling also threw a three. Baoqin laughed. “We had better confine ourselves to things in this room. If we include the world outside, there will be no clue where to begin.” “Naturally,” said Tanchun. Anyone who fails three times must drink a cup. You conceal the answer, and she guesses it.” Baoqin thought for a moment and offered the word “old.” Xiangling was unfamiliar with this game and could think of nothing at once. Looking all around the room and banquet table, she could see no object whose name formed an expression with the word “old.” On hearing the clue, Xiangyun also began looking about at random. Suddenly she noticed the three characters “Red Fragrance Garden” pasted above the doorway and realized that Baoqin had hidden the character “garden” from the phrase “I am not as good as an old gardener.” Seeing that Xiangling could not guess it while the others beat the drum and urged her on, Xiangyun quietly tugged at her and told her to say “medicine.” But Daiyu happened to see her and cried, “Quick, fine her! She is secretly passing on the answer over there.” Her cry made everyone aware of it, and they promptly fined Xiangyun another cup. Furious, Xiangyun tapped Daiyu's hand with her chopsticks. Xiangling was then fined a cup as well. Next, Baochai and Tanchun cast matching numbers. Tanchun gave the clue “man.” Baochai laughed. “This word ‘man’ is far too broad.” Tanchun laughed. “If I add one more word, giving you two clues for one guess, it will no longer be too broad.” With that, she added the word “window.”

p.src: Next, Baoyu happened to be paired with Baochai in the guessing game. Baochai gave the character “bao,” meaning “precious,” as her concealed clue. After a moment’s thought, Baoyu realized that she was playfully alluding to the Numinous Jade he wore, and laughed. “You have made an elegant jest of me, Sister, but I have guessed your answer. Do not be angry when I say it: the answer is the character in your own name, ‘chai.’” “How do you explain that?” everyone asked. Baoyu replied, “She said ‘bao,’ so naturally ‘yu’ comes after it. I guessed ‘chai’ because an old poem has the line, ‘The jade hairpin snapped beneath the tap; the red candle burned cold.’ Does that not prove I guessed correctly?” Xiangyun objected, “You cannot use present-day people and things as allusions. Both of you should be fined.” Xiangling hastened to say, “They are not merely present-day allusions; both have literary sources.” Xiangyun replied, “The two-character name ‘Baoyu’ has no literary source. It may appear in some New Year couplet, but it is nowhere recorded in the classics or poetry, so it does not count.” Xiangling said, “The other day I read a regulated five-character poem by Cen Jiazhou, and it contains the line, ‘This land abounds in precious jade.’ How can you have forgotten it? Later I read a seven-character quatrain by Li Yishan, which also has the line, ‘No day passes but the precious hairpin gathers dust.’ I even laughed and said that both their names had been in Tang poetry all along.” Everyone laughed. “She has silenced you this time. Quickly, drink a cup as your penalty!” Xiangyun had no reply and was obliged to drink. They resumed their diversions, some matching clues and others playing the finger-guessing drinking game. With Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang away, there was no one to restrain them. They amused themselves as they pleased, loudly calling out threes and fours, sevens and eights. Throughout the hall, crimson skirts flew and green sleeves danced, while jade and pearls swayed and shimmered—a truly splendid revel. At first they supposed she had stepped outside for some private need and would soon return, but the longer they waited, the less sign there was of her. Servants were sent to search everywhere, yet she was nowhere to be found.

They feared, first, that some important business might require attention, and second, that the young maids, with Lady Wang away, might refuse to heed Tanchun and the others, drink without restraint, and forget proper decorum. They had therefore come to ask whether anything was needed. p.src: They then selected several more kinds of fruit and vegetables to send to Xifeng, and she in turn sent several dishes back. Tanchun played a game of go with Baoqin, while Baochai and Xiuyan watched. Under a cluster of flowers, Lin Daiyu and Baoyu whispered together about no one knew what. Presently, Mrs. Lin Zhixiao appeared with a group of women, bringing a married servant woman with them. The woman looked thoroughly miserable and dared not enter the hall. On reaching the foot of the steps, she knelt toward those above and knocked her head audibly on the ground. One of Tanchun's groups had come under attack. After calculating every possibility, she saw that it could still make two eyes, so she abandoned the endgame move. Her eyes remained fixed on the board while one hand reached into the bowl and toyed endlessly with the stones as she pondered. Mrs. Lin Zhixiao had been standing there for some time before Tanchun noticed her when she turned to ask for tea. “What is it?” she asked. Mrs. Lin Zhixiao pointed to the woman. “This is the mother of Cai'er, the little maid in the Fourth Young Lady's rooms. She herself is employed here in the Garden. She has a vicious tongue. I happened to overhear her just now and questioned her, but what she said is too scandalous even to repeat to you, miss. She really ought to be driven out.” “Why didn't you report it to the Young Mistress?” asked Tanchun. “The Young Mistress had just gone to the hall to see Her Ladyship,” replied Mrs. Lin Zhixiao. “I met her on the way and reported everything, and she told me to come and report to you.” “Why didn't you report it to the Second Mistress?” asked Tanchun. “There is no need to go back and report it,” said Pinger. “I'll tell her when I return.” Tanchun nodded. “In that case, drive her out for now. When Her Ladyship returns, we shall report it and let her make the final decision.” With that, she resumed her game. Mrs. Lin Zhixiao led the woman away, and nothing more need be said of them. Though she has been put in charge of some affairs, she refuses to overstep her authority by so much as a single pace. Most people in her position would have begun throwing their weight around long ago.” “You don't know the half of it,” said Baoyu. While you were ill, she accomplished several important things. p.src: Baoyu laughed. “However short of funds they may become, there will always be enough for the two of us.” At this, Daiyu turned away and went into the hall to chat and laugh with Baochai. Just as Baoyu was about to leave, Xiren approached carrying a small linked-ring tray of foreign lacquer, on which two cups of freshly brewed tea stood neatly arranged. “Where has she gone?” she asked. “I saw that neither of you had drunk any tea for ages, so I specially poured two cups and brought them over, only for her to go away.” “There she is,” said Baoyu. “Take hers over to her.” As he spoke, he took one cup for himself. Xiren carried the other cup over, but Daiyu happened to be with Baochai. Since there was only one cup of tea, Xiren said, “Whichever of you is thirsty may have it first; I'll go and pour another.” Baochai laughed. “I'm not thirsty. One sip to rinse my mouth will be quite enough.” With that, she picked up the cup, took a sip, and handed the remaining half-cup to Daiyu. “I'll go and pour another,” said Xiren with a smile. Daiyu smiled. “You know about my illness. The doctor has forbidden me to drink too much tea, so this half-cup is more than enough. When we come back, I'll have Sister Xiren take you to eat at our table. How would that be?” “Ouguan and Ruiguan aren't going up there,” said Fangguan. “It wouldn't be right for me to be there alone. But if we drink tonight, no one is to keep watch over me. I mean to drink my fill before I stop. Before I came here, I could drink two or three catties of good Huiquan wine. Since I took up this wretched profession, they have said drinking would harm my voice, and for years I haven't even smelled wine. Today I'm going to break my abstinence.” “That is easily arranged,” said Baoyu.

p.src: Outside, Xiaoluo, Xiangling, Fangguan, Ruiguan, Ouguan, Douguan, and four or five others had been playing throughout the garden. They gathered flowers and grasses in their skirts, sat amid the heaps of greenery, and began a flower-matching game. p.src: Baoyu laughed. “You have a husband-and-wife cymbidium, while I happen to have a twin-blossomed water caltrop.” As he spoke, he really was holding a water-caltrop stem with twin blossoms. He also took the husband-and-wife cymbidium in his hand. Xiangling said, “Never mind husband and wife or twin blossoms. Just look at this skirt.” Only then did Baoyu look down. He cried, “Oh dear! How did it get dragged through the mud? What a shame—this pomegranate-red silk stains more easily than anything.” Xiangling said, “Miss Qin brought this cloth here the other day. Miss Bao had one skirt made, and I had another. Today was the first time I wore mine.” Baoyu stamped his foot and sighed. “In your household, even if a hundred such things were ruined in a day, it would be no great loss. But first of all, since Miss Qin brought the cloth and you and Cousin Bao had only one skirt made apiece, it would be a shame to disappoint her kindness when hers is still spotless and yours has already been stained. Second, Aunt Xue is inclined to grumble. Even as things are, I often hear her say that none of you knows how to manage a household, that you only know how to spoil things and never appreciate your good fortune. If Aunt Xue sees this, you will never hear the end of it.” Baoyu’s words touched precisely upon Xiangling’s concern, and instead she brightened and said with a smile, “That is exactly it. I do have several new skirts, but none is like this one. If I had an identical one and could change into it at once, everything would be all right. We could deal with the stained one afterward.” Baoyu said, “Do not move. You had better stand just as you are, or you will stain your undergarments, knee-breeches, and the uppers of your shoes as well. I have an idea. Xiren made a skirt last month exactly like this one, but since she is in mourning, she cannot wear it now. Why not have her give it to you so you can change out of this one?” Xiangling smiled, shook her head, and said, “That would not do. It would be awkward if the others heard about it.” Baoyu said, “Why should that matter? When her mourning is over, if there is something she likes, surely you can give her something else in return. If you refuse even this, it would hardly be like your usual generous self! Besides, there is no need to conceal it from anyone. You may tell Cousin Bao openly; we only need to keep Aunt Xue from becoming angry.” Xiangling considered this and found it reasonable. She nodded and said with a smile, “Very well, then. I would not want to disappoint your kindness. I will wait here for you, but make sure that she brings it herself.” Baoyu was delighted to hear this. He agreed and hurried back. As he went, he lowered his head and reflected, “What a pity that such a person should have no parents, should have forgotten even her own family name, should have been kidnapped and then, of all people, sold to that tyrant.” Then he recalled how the incident with Pinger the other day had also come about wholly by chance; what had happened today was even more unexpected than the unexpected.

p.src: Lost in a whirl of thoughts, Baoyu returned to his room, took Xiren aside, and told her the whole story in detail. There was no one who did not cherish Xiangling. Xiren was generous by nature, and she had always been on good terms with Xiangling. As soon as she heard the news, she opened her chest, took out the skirt, folded it neatly, and followed Baoyu to find Xiangling, who was still standing there waiting. Xiren laughed. “I always say you are far too mischievous—you are never satisfied until your pranks cause some great commotion.” Xiangling blushed and replied with a smile, “Thank you, sister. Who could have known those spiteful little mischief-makers would be so wicked?” As she spoke, she took the skirt and unfolded it. Sure enough, it was identical to her own. She then told Baoyu to turn his back, slipped her hands inside to untie the skirt she was wearing, and fastened this one around herself. Xiren said, “Give me the soiled one to take back. I will clean it up and bring it to you afterward. If you take it home yourself, they will question you when they see it.” Xiangling said, “Dear sister, take it away and give it to whichever of the younger girls you please. Now that I have this one, I no longer want the other.” “How very generous of you!” said Xiren. Xiangling hurriedly curtsied again in thanks, and Xiren left carrying the soiled skirt.

p.src: Xiangling saw Baoyu crouching on the ground. With a twig he had dug a hole for the husband-and-wife eupatorium and twin lotus she had shown him earlier. First he gathered some fallen petals to make a bed, then carefully laid the two flowers upon it, covered them with more fallen petals, and finally scooped earth over them and smoothed it flat. Xiangling took him by the hand and laughed. “And what do you call this? No wonder everyone says you are forever doing secretive, sentimental things that give people gooseflesh. Just look at your hands, black and slippery with mud! Go and wash them at once.” Baoyu rose with a smile and went to wash his hands, while Xiangling too walked away. After they had gone several paces, Xiangling turned back and called Baoyu to stop. Not knowing what she wanted to say, Baoyu held out his two muddy hands, turned back with a grin, and asked, “What is it?” Xiangling only laughed. Just then her little maid Zhen’er came over from the other side and said, “The Second Young Mistress is waiting to speak with you.” Only then did Xiangling say to Baoyu, “Please do not tell your elder cousin about the skirt.” With that, she turned and left. Baoyu laughed. “I would have to be mad indeed to stick my head into the tiger’s jaws!” As he spoke, he too went back to wash his hands.
